usage.result:
The three deliverables are in the folder: `build.py`, `weights.npz` (built from it) and `explanation.md`. The final network is the one that played the last practice round: it won 3 of 5 games, mean 1,649.

**Prediction for held-out games: about 1,600 on average**, with low confidence (80% range roughly 1,250 to 1,950). A game is close to all-or-nothing, about 2,277 for reaching the vest and a few hundred for dying on the way, and the last five versions each won 3 of 5.

How the network plays:
- **Shoot** when a monster is solidly on the crosshair, at any range. Monsters die to one shot and stay asleep until they can see the player, so half-hidden ones behind door frames get shot for free.
- **Turn** the heavier side onto the crosshair, with a deliberately lopsided rule (always for the right side, only when far out for the left). Held turns speed up to about 14° a step, and symmetric rules made the view flip left-right forever.
- **Otherwise** side-step towards a close monster, or walk on if it is far.
- **With no monster in view**, walk to the vest.

All ten practice rounds are used:

| Round | Mean | Wins |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1,968 | 4/5 |
| 2 | 660 | 1/5 |
| 3 | 1,321 | 3/5 |
| 4 | 1,852 | 4/5 |
| 5 | 1,064 | 2/5 |
| 6 | 1,491 | 3/5 |
| 7 | 1,524 | 3/5 |
| 8 | 1,546 | 3/5 |
| 9 | 1,571 | 3/5 |
| 10 (final) | 1,649 | 3/5 |

Rounds 1 and 4 scored higher than the final version, but the gap is within what five games can show. I kept the last version because it has no known way to get stuck; the earlier ones lost games to turn loops and to side-stepping against an invisible wall.

Known weaknesses of the final network:
- The opening fight costs about 25 health on average, sometimes over 40.
- A far monster just left of the crosshair is walked towards rather than shot; one such approach cost 42 health in the last round. I found no loop-safe turn rule for that case and had no practice rounds left to test one.
- Ammunition is not visible to the network, so very long fire
